clusters.title: Redis-secured hold can be left without durable state or recovery
clusters.description: A process/PostgreSQL failure after the atomic Redis stock decision leaves a real stock-consuming hold with no autonomous reconciliation path back to durable business state.

members.note: Reconciliation exists but is only reachable via another /buy and is cut off once run eligibility closes.
The pending-persistence sentinel is written only in a caught failure, so process exit leaves no obligation at all.
Even when the sentinel lands, reconciliation materializes a durable row without resolving the hold.
A PostgreSQL lookup outside the failure boundary and a failed sentinel write both escape as 500 with the secured hold invisible to the pending ledger.

clusters.title: Durable order commit can permanently outrun the BullMQ enqueue
clusters.description: Reservation/order rows commit before the queue handoff with no transactional outbox or background re-drive, so a failed or lost enqueue strands a durable queued order forever.

members.note: Additionally, maxRetriesPerRequest: null can leave the awaited enqueue hanging the request indefinitely.
The idempotent replay path returns early without re-attempting enqueue, so client retries cannot repair the handoff either.

clusters.title: ERP confirmation is not reliably idempotent
clusters.description: Duplicate deliveries of the same order confirmation are not safely deduplicated — via a racy check-then-store ledger, a non-durable ledger, or no idempotency contract at all — so the same business confirmation can apply twice.

members.note: Also flags loss of the ledger across process restart.
No idempotency barrier exists at all: a crash between ERP success and the attempt-row commit reuses the same attempt number and confirms again.

clusters.title: Unguarded start-phase transition races a fast completion
clusters.description: The run-start acknowledgement/promotion writes run state without an expected-state predicate, so a completion that lands first can be regressed or a terminal run resurrected.

members.note: A late start acknowledgement resurrects a draining or terminal run.
Unconditional markActive overwrites a fast draining/failed completion back to active.
The inverse loss: a fast completion is refused while the run still says starting and the missed transition is never replayed; the guarded activation result is also ignored against a concurrent reset.

clusters.title: Unreliable orchestrator-to-API completion handoff strands the run
clusters.description: The traffic-completion signal from the load orchestrator to the API is lossy (single attempt, swallowed failures, no durable retry), and only that signal can move the run out of active — so a transient failure strands the run and blocks later starts.

members.note: The receiver also acks accepted:true when its durable insert failed, so a delivered report can still finalize as a timeout failure.

clusters.title: Admin reset racing normal completion corrupts terminal run state
clusters.description: Reset reads a nonterminal run, loses the race to normal finalization, and then applies an unguarded failure transition that contradicts the already-written terminal outcome.

members.note: Reset can also admit and lose business state after the terminal summary is written.

clusters.title: Caller-supplied visitor identity bypasses public run budgets
clusters.description: The API trusts an unauthenticated caller-provided visitor identifier as the per-visitor budget key while being directly reachable, so rotating the header bypasses per-visitor limits.

notObserved.note: The review verified public budgets are enforced from a web-signed visitor identity the API cryptographically verifies and fails closed on; the observed failure mode is over-blocking (ir-F49), not bypass.

clusters.title: Live dashboard applies or retains data from a different run scope
clusters.description: The browser dashboard state does not consistently scope events/projections to the current run, so prior-run, catalog, or foreign-run data can be displayed as current.

members.note: A new-run event relabels projections retained from the previous scope.
Foreign-scope SSE events are applied before (or without) scope checking.
The reducer applies every valid event unconditionally; even an unrelated run's terminal event triggers a recovery.

clusters.title: Stale live dashboard state wins over newer authoritative data
clusters.description: Ordering/precedence in the live dashboard lets older data override newer authoritative state, so a missed or reordered event leaves the display permanently wrong.

members.note: Out-of-order same-run events overwrite newer state.
The retained live inventory overlay always beats the freshly recovered backend snapshot.
Reconnect recovery refreshes only the recovery object; inventory, queue, ERP, and lag panels keep their pre-disconnect values permanently.

clusters.title: Public dashboard read and SSE paths have no resource limits
clusters.description: Unauthenticated dashboard endpoints (SSE connections, history/read queries) have no connection caps, pagination, or rate limits, allowing unbounded resource consumption.

members.note: Unbounded SSE connection set.
Run History returns every summary without pagination.

clusters.title: Admin passphrase authentication permits unlimited online guesses
clusters.description: The public admin session route verifies every submitted passphrase with no rate limit, delay, or lockout, making the shared secret a cheap online oracle.

clusters.title: Web BFF error responses abandon the canonical error envelope
clusters.description: Proxy/BFF failure paths emit an error shape incompatible with the canonical API error contract, collapsing upstream details and correlation IDs into generic client messages.

members.note: Two incompatible web error families without correlation IDs, plus API-side SSE codes outside the shared vocabulary.

clusters.title: Test tooling can mutate a non-test database
clusters.description: Destructive or schema-mutating test commands rely on weak or missing target validation, so a mis-set environment can wipe or migrate development/shared data.

members.note: The PostgreSQL reset guard accepts unrelated names containing 'test'.
Redis FLUSHDB in integration suites has no target guard at all.
The isolated migration command can silently prefer an ambient development DATABASE_URL.
Truncate/FLUSHDB helpers act on whatever client they receive; the wrapper rejects only the two literal default ports.

clusters.title: Run cleanup can leave orphaned Redis state behind
clusters.description: Cleanup deletes or loses the durable mapping needed to clear the run's Redis namespaces, leaving eligibility/inventory keys orphaned after a partial failure or by design.

members.note: Old-run cleanup permanently leaves generated Redis namespaces behind.
PostgreSQL-first ordering makes a failed Redis cleanup unrecoverable.
Terminal-cleanup Redis DEL failures are swallowed and never retried; the poller only selects draining rows, so terminal runs are never repaired.

clusters.title: Cleanup and smoke teardown delete run state that is not settled or owned
clusters.description: By-id/old-run cleanup paths delete runs regardless of lifecycle status or ownership, and the load smoke invokes them on a fixed timer before business draining completes.

members.note: Load smoke tears down before draining completes.
Old-run cleanup deletes terminal state outside generated-run ownership.
By-id cleanup deletes an active run with jobs in flight after the smoke's fixed 3-second wait.
Admin reset tears down durable and Redis state and releases the one-run gate while the old k6 process keeps sending traffic.

clusters.title: Reference runtime does not enforce its control-plane secrets
clusters.description: The reference deployment boots and reports healthy without operator-provided secrets — either shipping public known defaults or tolerating their absence — leaving control endpoints and identity guarantees silently weakened.

members.note: Boots with public, known control credentials.
Boots healthy with the secrets missing entirely.
Only the web process validates production secrets; API, Mock ERP, and orchestrator fall back to committed tokens.

clusters.title: Root workspace test lanes silently omit application suites
clusters.description: The repo-root unit/watch/coverage commands cannot collect or run substantial parts of the per-package test suites, so the convenient top-level lanes give false coverage confidence.

members.note: Root watch omits every application unit suite.
Coverage excludes the highest-risk suites and enforces no floor.
Root unit/watch/coverage cannot run the web unit suite (missing alias, jsdom, TSX discovery).

clusters.title: No automated test exercises the deployed cross-service composition
clusters.description: Every automated suite substitutes doubles at the service boundaries, so the full suite can pass while the production API-to-queue-to-worker-to-ERP wiring is broken.

clusters.title: Finalization builds the immutable summary from best-effort reads instead of durable evidence
clusters.description: The terminal summary tolerates missing or unreadable delivery/inventory evidence at finalization time and still produces an authoritative record, instead of blocking on (or reusing) durable evidence that already exists.

members.note: A live Redis re-read replaces the already-durable terminal inventory snapshot; outages become permanent nulls.
Missing traffic evidence or a null k6 summary is graded complete.

clusters.title: Accepted run worker-concurrency policy is not actually honored
clusters.description: The backpressure/concurrency policy frozen into an accepted run is not reliably applied by the worker at execution time.

members.note: The reference worker cannot honor the two largest public presets' accepted concurrency.
Run-scoped concurrency is applied only after BullMQ has already admitted a default-sized batch.
Same late application, and the snapshot resolver additionally fails open to global defaults on errors.

clusters.title: Lifecycle boundary contracts validate values but not state coherence
clusters.description: Shared schemas at service boundaries reuse broad lifecycle enums and per-field checks without cross-field/state invariants, so impossible lifecycle payloads pass validation.

members.note: An 'active' completion and a 'failed' start acknowledgement both validate.
order.queued with toStatus confirmed and run.completed with status active both validate at the realtime gate.
Run History accepts an active summary and contradictory failure fields; the public preset schema accepts admin/editable rows.

clusters.title: Startup/restart reconciliation is one-shot and best-effort
clusters.description: Recovery-on-start swallows per-run errors and runs once, so a transient repair failure (or a partial view of an interrupted run) persists for the process lifetime.

members.note: Restart reconciliation freezes partial active-run outcomes as if final.
The immutable summary is written from a point-in-time read with zero sold-out counts and no terminal snapshot, then the Redis-only accounting is destroyed.

clusters.title: Correlation IDs are not propagated across the whole request chain
clusters.description: Parts of the observability chain mint fresh correlation IDs or omit them instead of inheriting the initiating request's ID, breaking end-to-end traceability.

members.note: Routine HTTP logs do not inherit the request correlation ID.
The orchestrator drops the run-start correlation ID for background work and callbacks.
Run IDs are bound as correlationId, fabricating traces and discarding the admin-reset request correlation.

clusters.title: An unexpected throw during the half-open probe wedges the circuit breaker
clusters.description: The single half-open probe flag is released only when a result is recorded; a non-ERP error thrown through the wrapper never records success or failure, so the breaker stays half-open with a permanently in-flight probe until process restart.

members.note: Reproduced with the shipped modules; while wedged, ir-F7 permanently fails every picked-up order.

clusters.title: Awaited dashboard publication sits on the synchronous buy path
clusters.description: Best-effort realtime/dashboard publication is awaited before the buy response returns, adding observability latency and fan-out load to the hot path the design says must stay cheap.

members.note: The accepted path awaits Redis PUBLISH without a timeout.
Every sold-out loser awaits its own publication, contradicting the documented aggregate-only sold-out path.

clusters.title: Idempotency keys are unbounded and amplified into Redis
clusters.description: The shared idempotency-key schema accepts any non-empty string and the buy path embeds it in Redis keys and stored values with a long TTL, so large keys amplify memory and bandwidth on the critical path.

clusters.title: PostgreSQL accepts child rows that contradict the parent they describe
clusters.description: Orders, ERP attempts, and related child rows duplicate run/offer/correlation identity with only a single foreign key and no agreement or status/timestamp constraints, so the durable source of truth accepts impossible histories.

members.note: Same class observed at lower severity: attribution integrity rests mostly on application discipline.

clusters.title: Grading every HTTP 409 as expected traffic hides lifecycle failures
clusters.description: The generated k6 script marks the whole 409 status class expected while the buy path also uses 409 for closed runs, missing eligibility, and idempotency conflicts — so a completely broken run can report clean traffic delivery.

clusters.title: Generated run-sale ownership can be invalidated after guarded insertion
clusters.description: Run and sale-context rows store sale-offer ownership independently with guards firing only at insertion, so a later contradictory write (offer purpose or pointer change) silently invalidates the ownership relationship downstream code trusts.

members.note: Demonstrated at the storage boundary by the branch's own maintenance test, which flips a context-owned offer to catalog.

clusters.title: Worker readiness reports healthy without probing its dependencies
clusters.description: The worker readiness endpoint maps configuration presence or process-local object state to healthy without any real PostgreSQL/Redis round trip, so orchestration and monitoring stay green while no order can actually be processed.

members.note: Also covers the consumer check, which reports BullMQ object lifecycle rather than connectivity.

clusters.title: Frozen snapshots and immutable summaries are ordinary updateable rows
clusters.description: Run config snapshots and terminal summaries are treated as immutable by the application but PostgreSQL enforces neither update rejection nor content validity, so out-of-band writes can rewrite history that readers trust without re-validation.

members.note: The read adapter also casts summary JSONB without parsing, so a mutated row is served as if valid.

clusters.title: Process-local run state has no retention bound
clusters.description: Long-lived services accumulate per-run in-memory state (execution maps, idempotency ledgers, semaphores) that is never evicted, growing without bound across hosted runs.

clusters.title: The only real-k6 verification is optional and skipped by standard gates
clusters.description: The single test lane that exercises real generated-script/k6 compatibility is either skipped when the binary is absent or omitted from the root suite entirely, so k6 incompatibility regressions survive every standard automated check.

members.note: The lane exists but pnpm test never invokes it, and it is not runnable in the documented reference setup (k6 lives only in the orchestrator image).

clusters.title: Test-source type checking is declared but not effective
clusters.description: A type-check:test command exists in the workspace contract but either resolves to zero package tasks or is invoked by no gate, so test-only TypeScript errors and fixture drift hide behind green checks.

members.note: The command exists and currently fails, but no gate invokes it.
The command exists but no package defines the script, so it exits 0 having checked nothing.

clusters.title: Documented environment configuration is silently inert in the reference runtime
clusters.description: Documented environment variables — deployment caps, policy defaults, service tuning — are either never parsed by the owning process or never forwarded by Compose, so operator overrides silently do nothing.

members.note: Compose puts policy overrides on a process that does not read them while the seed-owning setup service receives none.
Compose forwards only a small fixed subset, including giving the shared cookie secret to web but not the API that verifies it.
The documented DEMO_MAX_* deployment caps are never parsed; validation silently uses compile-time constants.
One facet of a broader finding: public-policy env defaults are hard-coded and never passed to the setup job.

clusters.title: Streamed k6 metrics are converted to live rates with a wrong denominator
clusters.description: Live request/failure rates are derived from streamed k6 samples without a correct time-window denominator — raw points forwarded as rates, or partial windows divided by the full polling interval — so the headline live rate misstates actual traffic.

clusters.title: Purchases remain accepted after the sale's eligibility window closes
clusters.description: The hot-path acceptance gate is not closed in step with the sale's lifecycle — offers or runs whose window has ended keep accepting fresh reservations until a later, best-effort projection update lands.

members.note: Catalog offers with stale initialized inventory are authorized after their active/start/end window.
Draining and even terminal runs keep accepting fresh reservations until finalization's late eligibility clear succeeds.

clusters.title: The drain timeout mishandles unsettled business work
clusters.description: When the drain timeout fires with business work still unsettled, finalization takes a wrong branch — either retrying reconciliation forever and blocking new runs, or bypassing the settlement gate and recording the run as completed.

members.note: Unbounded post-timeout reconciliation leaves the run draining and blocks new starts.
The timeout bypasses the settlement gate and labels a run with processing orders completed in an immutable summary.

clusters.title: Queue-attempt exhaustion leaves durable orders permanently processing
clusters.description: When BullMQ exhausts a job's retry budget there is no durable dead-letter or compensation path, so the order stays in processing forever, run finalization waits for the drain timeout, and the failure is invisible to business state.

members.note: ERP-attempt persistence failures are one path that exhausts the budget.
The strongest real-BullMQ integration test explicitly asserts the stranded-processing result.
